title: Historical-to-future pattern-effect correction
subfield: Radiative forcing, clouds, and climate sensitivity
open: Predict how geographical patterns of ocean warming change global radiative feedback. Infer long-term sensitivity from historical observations without prescribing the uncertain future sea-surface-temperature pattern.
status: Intensive work since the 2010s demonstrates substantial historical effective-sensitivity biases in model experiments; the real-world correction remains uncertain.
why: Connects observed warming rates to future warming.
key_works: Gregory et al. (2020; online 2019), [“How accurately can the climate sensitivity to CO₂ be estimated from historical climate change?”](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00382-019-04991-y).

title: Transferable trade-cumulus feedback constraints
subfield: Radiative forcing, clouds, and climate sensitivity
open: Determine trade-cumulus feedback across seasons, basins, mesoscale organizations, and warmer climates. Establish which observed cloud–circulation relationships remain valid as environmental conditions change.
status: EUREC4A observations reported in 2022 refuted strong mixing-desiccation feedback in sampled conditions and supported weak feedback; broader transfer remains open.
why: Tests an influential mechanism producing high simulated climate sensitivity.
key_works: Vogel et al. (2022), [“Strong cloud–circulation coupling explains weak trade cumulus feedback”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-022-05364-y).

title: Tropical anvil optical-depth feedback
subfield: Radiative forcing, clouds, and climate sensitivity
open: Determine how warming changes tropical-anvil ice mass, particle sizes, optical depth, and life cycles. Quantify the resulting shortwave-plus-longwave feedback separately from changes in anvil area.
status: McKim and colleagues substantially constrained the area contribution in 2024 while identifying anvil albedo feedback as unresolved.
why: Resolves a cloud-feedback component affecting warming projections.
key_works: McKim, Bony and Dufresne (2024), [“Weak anvil cloud area feedback suggested by physical and observational constraints”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41561-024-01414-4).

title: Attribution of the recent planetary-albedo decline
subfield: Radiative forcing, clouds, and climate sensitivity
open: Separate aerosol changes, internal ocean variability, and temperature-driven cloud feedback in declining reflected sunlight. Close attribution against spectral radiation, cloud properties, ocean-temperature patterns, and heat uptake.
status: Goessling and colleagues linked the 2023 temperature surge to exceptionally low albedo, especially reduced low-cloud cover; the cloud-change causes remained unresolved.
why: Distinguishes persistent feedback and forcing changes from transient variability.
key_works: Goessling, Rackow and Jung (2025; online 2024), [“Recent global temperature surge intensified by record-low planetary albedo”](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adq7280).

title: Convective self-aggregation in the real tropical atmosphere
open: Determine when spontaneous aggregation in idealized radiative-convective equilibrium controls observed tropical organization. Predict dependence on temperature, rotation, domain size, shear, and surface coupling.
status: Studied since the 1990s; RCEMIP reproduced aggregation across many models in 2020 but exposed substantial disagreement under standardized conditions.
why: Connects mesoscale storms with humidity, radiation, and precipitation extremes.
key_works: Wing et al. (2020), [“Clouds and Convective Self-Aggregation in a Multimodel Ensemble of Radiative-Convective Equilibrium Simulations”](https://doi.org/10.1029/2020MS002138).

title: Scale-aware entrainment and detrainment closure
open: Derive cloud–environment exchange laws that work from shallow cumulus through deep convection as resolution changes. Predict dilution and mass-flux profiles without regime-specific retuning.
status: A decades-old problem; large-eddy simulations constrain cases, but organized exchange and turbulent mixing remain difficult to generalize.
why: Improves rainfall, cloud feedback, and tropical circulation together.
key_works: de Rooy et al. (2013), [“Entrainment and detrainment in cumulus convection: an overview”](https://doi.org/10.1002/qj.1959).

title: A discriminating theory of the Madden–Julian oscillation
open: Identify mechanisms setting MJO initiation, eastward propagation, scale, and termination. Derive observations that distinguish competing moisture, wave, and ocean-coupling theories, including Maritime Continent passage.
status: Open since discovery in 1971–1972; theories reproduce important features, but the 2020 fifty-year assessment retained major mechanism and prediction questions.
why: Extends useful prediction of tropical rainfall and remote extremes.
key_works: Jiang et al. (2020), [“Fifty Years of Research on the Madden-Julian Oscillation: Recent Progress, Challenges, and Perspectives”](https://doi.org/10.1029/2019JD030911).

title: Forced changes in ENSO diversity and amplitude
open: Quantify warming-driven changes in eastern- versus central-Pacific El Niño, La Niña persistence, amplitude, and transition probabilities. Separate forced change from multidecadal variability.
status: Decades of research; Cai et al. (2021) synthesized increasing evidence for stronger variability in selected models, with quantitative projections still uncertain.
why: Governs connected drought, flood, ecosystem, and agricultural hazards.
key_works: Cai et al. (2021), [“Changing El Niño–Southern Oscillation in a warming climate”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43017-021-00199-z).

title: Tropical Pacific observed–modeled trend discrepancy
open: Explain discrepancies between observed multidecadal equatorial Pacific temperature-gradient changes and coupled-model responses. Discriminate internal variability, dynamical biases, aerosol forcing, and observational errors.
status: Persistent across model generations; Seager et al. (2022) documented discrepancies extending beyond individual ENSO events.
why: Pacific warming patterns shape global feedback and regional drought.
key_works: Seager, Henderson and Cane (2022), [“Persistent Discrepancies between Observed and Modeled Trends in the Tropical Pacific Ocean”](https://doi.org/10.1175/JCLI-D-21-0648.1).

title: The climate signal-to-noise paradox
open: Explain why some initialized ensembles predict observations better than their apparent predictable signal implies. Identify and correct weak responses, excessive noise, sampling, or ensemble-construction causes.
status: Prominent since 2014; formalized in 2018; a 2024 community reassessment found no conclusive general resolution.
why: Could unlock additional seasonal and decadal forecast skill.
key_works: Scaife and Smith (2018), [“A signal-to-noise paradox in climate science”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-018-0038-4); Weisheimer et al. (2024), [“The Signal-to-Noise Paradox in Climate Forecasts: Revisiting Our Understanding and Identifying Future Priorities”](https://doi.org/10.1175/BAMS-D-24-0019.1).

title: Global closure of boundary-driven abyssal upwelling
open: Determine how much deep-water upwelling occurs in thin turbulent boundary layers along slopes. Scale local observations to basin transports while closing the energy budget.
status: A 2024 dye experiment directly observed strong diapycnal upwelling in one submarine canyon; global prevalence and parameterization remain open.
why: Connects small-scale mixing to global overturning.
key_works: Wynne-Cattanach et al. (2024), [“Observations of diapycnal upwelling within a sloping submarine canyon”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07411-2).

title: Conditions for self-sustaining marine ice-cliff failure
subfield: Ice sheets, glaciers, and sea ice
open: Determine when cliff failure can outrun viscous thinning, mélange buttressing, and geometric stabilization. Establish observationally constrained conditions for sustained retreat.
status: Influential since the 2010s; Morlighem et al. (2024) found stabilizing processes can prevent MICI in modeled twenty-first-century settings.
why: Tests a proposed contributor to high-end sea-level projections.
key_works: Morlighem et al. (2024), [“The West Antarctic Ice Sheet may not be vulnerable to marine ice cliff instability during the 21st century”](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.ado7794).

title: Three-dimensional solid-Earth feedback on Antarctic retreat
subfield: Ice sheets, glaciers, and sea ice
open: Infer mantle viscosity and lithospheric structure sufficiently to jointly predict unloading, uplift, gravitational changes, water redistribution, and ice retreat.
status: Gomez et al. (2024) showed realistic three-dimensional structure materially changes projected sea levels; that structure remains incompletely observed.
why: Rebound affects both ice stability and regional sea-level fingerprints.
key_works: Gomez et al. (2024), [“The influence of realistic 3D mantle viscosity on Antarctica’s contribution to future global sea levels”](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.adn1470).

title: Persistence and reversibility of the Antarctic low-sea-ice state
subfield: Ice sheets, glaciers, and sea ice
open: Determine whether recent behavior represents a persistent transition, a long-lived forced response, or unusual variability. Identify physical conditions permitting recovery.
status: The question sharpened after 2016; Raphael et al. (2025) found structural statistical change, which alone does not demonstrate irreversible bifurcation.
why: Affects Southern Ocean heat exchange, ecosystems, and projections.
key_works: Raphael et al. (2025), [“A twenty-first century structural change in Antarctica’s sea ice system”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43247-025-02107-5).

title: Definition-robust atmospheric-river change estimates
open: Establish which changes in occurrence, duration, clustering, and landfall survive reasonable detection definitions. Translate definitions into physically interpretable transport and impact statistics.
status: ARTMIP compared over twenty tracking methods in 2019 and found substantial methodological dependence.
why: Prevents event-label choices from dominating flood and water projections.
key_works: Rutz et al. (2019), [“The Atmospheric River Tracking Method Intercomparison Project (ARTMIP): Quantifying Uncertainties in Atmospheric River Climatology”](https://doi.org/10.1029/2019JD030936).

title: Unique causal explanation of the Mid-Pleistocene Transition
open: Determine why glacial cycles shifted from predominantly 41,000-year to larger, roughly 100,000-year rhythms without comparable orbital-forcing change. Discriminate ice, regolith, ocean, and CO₂ mechanisms.
status: Willeit et al. (2019) reproduced the transition using CO₂ decline and regolith removal, establishing model sufficiency without unique historical causation.
why: Tests nonlinear ice–climate feedbacks and long-term transitions.
key_works: Willeit et al. (2019), [“Mid-Pleistocene transition in glacial cycles explained by declining CO₂ and regolith removal”](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aav7337).

title: Absolute radiometric closure of Earth’s energy imbalance
open: Sustain radiation measurements accurate and continuous enough to independently resolve changes in planetary energy imbalance. Close calibration, sampling, and radiance-to-flux errors against heat storage.
status: A decades-old metrology challenge; CLARREO established an SI-traceable approach, while heat inventories provide complementary constraints.
why: Measures whether planetary heat accumulation is accelerating.
key_works: Wielicki et al. (2013), [“Achieving Climate Change Absolute Accuracy in Orbit”](https://doi.org/10.1175/BAMS-D-12-00149.1).

title: Attribution of the residual land carbon sink
open: Separate CO₂ fertilization, nutrient deposition, climate, regrowth, and management contributions to regional uptake. Predict withheld fluxes and vegetation-versus-soil storage consistently.
status: A decades-old problem; O’Sullivan et al. (2022) showed globally agreeing models diverge in processes and regional responses.
why: Determines future vegetation and soil uptake of emissions.
key_works: O’Sullivan et al. (2022), [“Process-oriented analysis of dominant sources of uncertainty in the land carbon sink”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-32416-8).

title: Nutrient-limited CO₂ fertilization in mature forests
open: Predict how nitrogen and phosphorus constrain conversion of additional photosynthesis into persistent carbon. Test whole-ecosystem allocation across forest types with multiyear manipulations.
status: Jiang et al. (2020) found additional assimilation largely returned through respiration in mature eucalyptus forest; transfer across forests remains unresolved.
why: Resolves a major uncertainty in the future land sink.
key_works: Jiang et al. (2020), [“The fate of carbon in a mature forest under carbon dioxide enrichment”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2128-9).

title: Amazon forest transition thresholds under interacting stresses
open: Determine location-dependent thresholds for persistent forest loss under warming, drying, deforestation, and fire. Distinguish local degradation from self-sustaining regional moisture-recycling transitions.
status: Flores et al. (2024) synthesized candidate thresholds; their ranges do not constitute validated basin-scale transition forecasts.
why: Identifies interventions preserving carbon, biodiversity, and rainfall.
key_works: Flores et al. (2024), [“Critical transitions in the Amazon forest system”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06970-0).

title: Independent measurement of global OH variability
open: Constrain methane-weighted hydroxyl abundance independently of methane observations used to infer emissions. Separate OH variability from tracer-emission and transport uncertainty.
status: A decades-old attribution obstacle; the 2022 analysis of 2020 illustrates material sink effects on inferred source growth.
why: Makes methane verification robust to changing atmospheric cleansing.
key_works: Peng et al. (2022), [“Wetland emission and atmospheric sink changes explain methane growth in 2020”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-022-05447-w).

title: Annual methane budgets for intermittent super-emitters
open: Infer annual methane totals from brief, irregular observations when rare events dominate. Establish duration distributions, detection probabilities, and calibrated uncertainty across operating regimes.
status: Lauvaux et al. (2022) mapped global oil-and-gas ultra-emitters; snapshots do not establish annual intermittent-source totals.
why: Verifies repair benefits between satellite overpasses.
key_works: Lauvaux et al. (2022), [“Global assessment of oil and gas methane ultra-emitters”](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abj4351).

title: Whole-profile carbon additionality of reduced tillage
open: Identify conditions producing additional whole-profile carbon after accounting for density, erosion, yields, and other gases. Distinguish redistribution from persistent stock increases.
status: Powlson et al. (2014) showed many apparent benefits reflect depth redistribution; conditional prediction remains open.
why: Prevents overstated removals and identifies effective management.
key_works: Powlson et al. (2014), [“Limited potential of no-till agriculture for climate change mitigation”](https://doi.org/10.1038/nclimate2292).

title: Biological nitrification inhibition across real agricultural soils
open: Breed crops whose inhibitors suppress harmful nitrification across soil, microbiome, and fertilizer conditions without yield loss. Demonstrate reduced combined N₂O, leaching, and ammonia losses.
status: Subbarao et al. (2021) transferred the trait into wheat; consistent whole-system performance remains unresolved.
why: Provides a crop-encoded route to better nitrogen efficiency.
key_works: Subbarao et al. (2021), [“Enlisting wild grass genes to combat nitrification in wheat farming: A nature-based solution”](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2106595118).

title: DAC sorbent lifetime under real ambient contaminants
open: Demonstrate sorbents retaining capacity and regeneration efficiency through years of oxygen, humidity, aerosol, and pollutant exposure. Validate accelerated aging against field degradation.
status: Zhou et al. (2024) demonstrated over 100 open-air cycles for COF-999; multiyear commercial lifetime remains unestablished.
why: Replacement costs and embodied emissions can dominate performance.
key_works: Zhou et al. (2024), [“Carbon dioxide capture from open air using covalent organic frameworks”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08080-x).

title: Field-scale basalt dissolution-rate prediction
open: Predict dissolution of crushed basalt applied to agricultural soils from mineralogy, particle size, acidity, wetting, biology, and passivation. Validate across multiyear sites.
status: Beerling et al. (2024) reported a replicated four-year Corn Belt trial; broader long-duration validation remains necessary.
why: Determines processing requirements and removal timing.
key_works: Beerling et al. (2024), [“Enhanced weathering in the US Corn Belt delivers carbon removal with agronomic benefits”](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2319436121).

title: OAE atmospheric uptake before water-mass subduction
open: Verify atmospheric uptake following alkalinity addition before treated water subducts. Quantify location, season, circulation, and re-emergence effects over stated crediting horizons.
status: Zhou et al. (2025) mapped strong modeled geographical variation; independently validated project-scale uptake remains a gap.
why: Added alkalinity is potential capacity until atmospheric uptake occurs.
key_works: Zhou et al. (2025), [“Mapping the global variation in the efficiency of ocean alkalinity enhancement for carbon dioxide removal”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-024-02179-9).

title: Avoiding runaway carbonate precipitation during OAE
open: Predict dose, dilution, particles, and environmental conditions triggering precipitation. Develop controls preserving alkalinity at operationally useful concentrations and flows.
status: Suitner et al. (2024) measured contrasting stability windows over 20–25 days; transfer across environments remains unresolved.
why: Precipitation can consume added alkalinity and erase removal.
key_works: Suitner et al. (2024), [“Ocean alkalinity enhancement approaches and the predictability of runaway precipitation processes: results of an experimental study to determine critical alkalinity ranges for safe and sustainable application scenarios”](https://doi.org/10.5194/bg-21-4587-2024).

title: Residence time and ecological consequences of sunk seaweed
open: Determine biomass fate through fragmentation, grazing, decomposition, and circulation. Identify conditions providing century-scale atmospheric isolation without unacceptable oxygen depletion or ecosystem damage.
status: Modeled farming potential and release depth do not establish site-specific permanence or ecological consequences.
why: Determines whether sinking delivers durable removal.
key_works: Bach et al. (2021), [“Testing the climate intervention potential of ocean afforestation using the Great Atlantic Sargassum Belt”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-22837-2); DeAngelo et al. (2023), [“Economic and biophysical limits to seaweed farming for climate change mitigation”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41477-022-01305-9).

title: Basalt mineralization with low freshwater demand
open: Achieve rapid verified mineralization of injected CO₂ using little freshwater or suitable saline water while preserving injectivity across heterogeneous reservoirs.
status: Matter et al. (2016) demonstrated rapid Icelandic mineralization; broader water chemistry and reservoir transfer remain open.
why: Expands durable storage beyond favorable demonstration sites.
key_works: Matter et al. (2016), [“Rapid carbon mineralization for permanent disposal of anthropogenic carbon dioxide emissions”](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aad8132).

title: Prospective control of geothermal induced seismicity
open: Forecast damaging-earthquake probabilities early enough to adjust injection, including delayed events after shut-in. Validate calibration prospectively at unseen sites.
status: Adaptive traffic-light models and retrospective forecasts provide partial results; transferable prospective control remains unestablished.
why: Protects communities and prevents project-ending seismicity.
key_works: Mignan et al. (2017), [“Induced seismicity closed-form traffic light system for actuarial decision-making during deep fluid injections”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-13585-9).

title: Durable kilowatt-scale elastocaloric refrigeration
open: Deliver kilowatt cooling at useful temperature lift with competitive system efficiency, low noise, and long fatigue life, including pumps, drives, and replacements.
status: Zhou et al. (2025) reported 1,284 W at zero lift over the initial 500,000 cycles; useful-lift integrated lifetime remains open.
why: Could provide cooling without conventional volatile refrigerants.
key_works: Zhou et al. (2025), [“Achieving kilowatt-scale elastocaloric cooling by a multi-cell architecture”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08549-9).

title: Contrail avoidance with verified net climate benefit
open: Execute route changes reducing warming after contrail lifetime, radiation, fuel penalties, forecast errors, and traffic constraints. Verify prospectively across seasons and regions.
status: A 2024 randomized commercial-flight trial demonstrated avoidance with measurable fuel penalties; robust global climate benefit remains open.
why: Offers operational mitigation before fleet replacement.
key_works: Sonabend-W et al. (2024), [“Feasibility test of per-flight contrail avoidance in commercial aviation”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44172-024-00329-7).

title: Heat pumps above 250°C
open: Deliver industrial heat above 250°C with efficient lift, durable compressors, stable fluids, and competitive installed cost across variable loads.
status: Lower-temperature systems are established; Yoo et al. (2025) identify substantial higher-temperature gaps.
why: Electrifies process heat while recovering waste heat.
key_works: Yoo, Estrada-Perez and Choi (2025), [“Investigation of heat pump technologies for high-temperature applications above 250°C”](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apenergy.2025.125384).

title: Flexible electric steam cracking
open: Operate through realistic power variations without excessive coking, fatigue, or selectivity changes. Validate commercial-throughput integration.
status: A 6-MW BASF–SABIC–Linde demonstrator started in 2024; flexible lifetime economics remain open.
why: Removes furnace combustion from major chemical production.
key_works: BASF (2024–2025), [“Climate-smart technologies”](https://www.basf.com/global/en/who-we-are/sustainability/our-contributions-to-enabling-the-green-transformation/climate-protection/climate-smart-technologies).

title: Copper and tin removal from steel scrap
open: Remove tramp copper and tin economically enough to produce demanding grades without routine dilution with primary iron.
status: Daehn et al. quantified the copper constraint in 2017; sorting and specialized refining provide partial solutions.
why: Enables repeated high-quality steel recycling.
key_works: Daehn, Serrenho and Allwood (2017), [“How Will Copper Contamination Constrain Future Global Steel Recycling?”](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.7b00997).

title: Efficient, contamination-proof electrochemical nitrogen fixation
open: Reduce N₂ to ammonia at useful rate, system efficiency, and durability with rigorously closed nitrogen and reagent balances.
status: Andersen et al. (2019) established isotope validation; lithium-mediated advances do not settle full-process competitiveness.
why: Could enable distributed clean fertilizer synthesis.
key_works: Andersen et al. (2019), [“A rigorous electrochemical ammonia synthesis protocol with quantitative isotope measurements”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-1260-x).

title: Methane pyrolysis without dependence on premium carbon markets
open: Continuously separate carbon without fouling and prove low emissions and viable economics when carbon requires durable storage rather than specialty sales.
status: Upham et al. demonstrated molten-metal pyrolysis in 2017; upstream leakage and bulk-carbon handling remain decisive constraints.
why: Tests scalable low-emission hydrogen production.
key_works: Upham et al. (2017), [“Catalytic molten metals for the direct conversion of methane to hydrogen and separable carbon”](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29146810/).

title: Industrial olefin–paraffin separation without distillation
subfield: Point-source capture, geological storage, and circular materials
open: Produce polymer-grade ethylene or propylene using durable low-energy membranes or adsorbents under real impurities, cycling, and throughput.
status: Longstanding; Sholl and Lively highlighted the target in 2016. Laboratory selectivity has not settled economical cyclic operation.
why: Cuts recurring petrochemical energy demand.
key_works: Sholl and Lively (2016), [“Seven chemical separations to change the world”](https://doi.org/10.1038/532435a).

title: Independently verified annual facility CO₂ emissions from space
subfield: Climate policy, finance, institutions, and accountability
open: Infer annual power-plant and industrial-process CO₂ totals despite clouds, sparse overpasses, production variation, neighboring sources, and uncertain winds. Validate against continuous measurements.
status: Nassar et al. demonstrated selected daily estimates in 2017; reliable global annual totals require further progress.
why: Provides independent checks on major emitters.
key_works: Nassar et al. (2017), [“Quantifying CO₂ Emissions From Individual Power Plants From Space”](https://doi.org/10.1002/2017GL074702).

title: Fifteen-year superhot geothermal wells
open: Develop wells, seals, sensors, and fluid systems operating above 375°C and 22 MPa for at least fifteen years despite cycling and corrosion.
status: Superhot resources have been accessed experimentally; ARPA-E’s 2025 SUPERHOT program targets sustained-production durability.
why: Could increase heat extraction per well substantially.
key_works: ARPA-E (2025), [“SUPERHOT”](https://arpa-e.energy.gov/programs-and-initiatives/view-all-programs/superhot).
